messages:
Customer Success - Claire: Heads-up — AcmeOps (Sam) reports subtle shortening/trim in model replies after yesterday's hosted rollout (model v1.9.2). They provided before/after samples and are worried about missed clarifying steps.

AcmeOps - Sam (customer): example attached, we saw this after 03/16 ~09:12 UTC. Not a correctness bug, more of a tone/length regression — answers feel clipped and skip follow-ups.

Aisha (support): Can you paste the samples here so eng can eyeball? Also need the request_id and call params.

AcmeOps - Sam (customer): sure — request_id: r_01FZ9ABCD1234, region: us-east-1, model: redwood-text-1.9.2, params: {"max_tokens": 180, "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95}. Samples: 

```
Prompt: "How do I reset the API key for a user?"
Before (v1.8.7): "You can reset the API key from the console: Settings -> API Keys. Click 'Rotate', confirm, then update any integrations to use the new key. If you want I can give a curl example to update keys programmatically."
After (v1.9.2): "Go to Settings > API Keys and rotate it."
```

Aisha (support): Thanks. That's pretty pared down — customer says multiple prompts show similar "drop of scaffolding" (no next steps, no offer to help).

Ben (eng-ml): Noted. We didn't intentionally change any generation defaults for hosted models. @Rowan any infra/packaging changes yesterday?

Rowan (eng-runtime): We pushed rollout-2026-03-16-v1.9.2 at 09:08 UTC. It included a quantization packaging fix and a minor decoder patch to improve throughput. Canary at 10% then promoted. eng_bot logged: "deploy rollout-2026-03-16-v1.9.2 -> hosted (canary 10%) at 2026-03-16T09:08:21Z; promoted to 100% at 2026-03-16T09:12:03Z".

Ben (eng-ml): Packaging fix shouldn't change decoding, but the decoder patch might tweak stop-token handling/early termination heuristics. Can you point me to the exact diff?

Rowan (eng-runtime): PR #4821 — small change in the end-of-sequence scoring to reduce hallucinated tails. It biases earlier termination by ~0.5 token on median per our perf tests.

Ben (eng-ml): That could explain the trimming. It matches symptoms: shorter outputs, fewer optional clarifications. I'll run comparator: same prompt across v1.8.7 vs v1.9.2 with the customer's params.

Aisha (support): Customer is asking for rollback if this is intentional and causes UX regression. They want a timeline and mitigation.

Customer Success - Claire: Sam says it's impacting workflows (support flows rely on step-by-step guidance). They asked for repro steps for us to run and a screenshot of differences.

Ben (eng-ml): Quick repro snippet I'll use locally: 
```
# curl example
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-text-1.9.2","prompt":"How do I reset the API key for a user?","max_tokens":180,"temperature":0.2}'
```
I'll run N=50 for seed variability and compare token-length distribution + presence of follow-up sentences.

Rowan (eng-runtime): I'll also pull logs for request_id r_01FZ9ABCD1234 and inspect any prefix trimming or kv-cache truncation that could be cutting off generator context.

eng_bot: audit-log: rollout-2026-03-16-v1.9.2 -> changeset includes: decoder-eos-bias (delta +0.5), packaging-fix (no runtime config changes).

Ben (eng-ml): If the decoder eos-bias is the culprit we can revert that small scoring tweak for hosted until we do a deeper QA. Impact looks like ~7-12% median token reduction for short-guidance prompts based on initial sims.

Aisha (support): Ok please confirm ETA for either a patch or rollback and I'll tell the customer. They asked explicitly for: 1) temporary rollback 2) or config toggle to disable eos-bias on their account.

Rowan (eng-runtime): Rollback path: re-promote previous canary (v1.8.7 build) — risk low. Can do within 30-45 minutes if eng approves. Alternative: add per-tenant config to disable eos-bias but that's longer.

Ben (eng-ml): I'll finish the comparator in 20m and post metrics + example diffs. If it matches, I support rollback.

Customer Success - Claire: Thanks. Sam — I'll ask for any more examples and let you know timeline.

AcmeOps - Sam (customer): appreciate the quick triage. Please keep me posted. :) :thumbsup:

Aisha (support): tagging @product for visibility — product may want to log this as a quality regression.

[end of thread]
